exposure: maternal blood group (A, B, AB, O) with negative Rhesus
Anti-D serum infusion (single infusion during first pregnancy)
outcome: clinical characteristics of fetomaternal Rhesus incompatibility
cohort: The study included 37 pregnant women with blood groups A, B, AB, or O and a negative Rhesus factor, and 30 newborns with fetomaternal Rhesus incompatibility identified from 11,898 pregnant women admitted to a maternity hospital over a 4-year period.
finding: The prevalence of fetomaternal Rhesus incompatibility was found to be 0.31% among pregnant women, with 30 cases recorded in newborns, and 12 (40%) of these newborns developed jaundice.
cross-section timing: Data was collected retrospectively over a 4-year period.
